mainTopic: Showing honor and conducting a meal properly: deferring at doorways, waiting for the בוצע, answering אמן, who leads the זימון, and the משנה's cases of דמאי and מעשר ראשון
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא: we do not make a show of letting a greater person go first on roads, on bridges, or at the after-meal hand-washing. In a story, רבין does not defer to אביי on the road but does at the בית הכנסת door, explaining with רבי יוחנן's rule that we defer only at a doorway fit for a מזוזה. The גמרא then turns to honor at a meal: guests wait until the בוצע tastes the bread, and רב ספרא teaches that a student must repeat his teacher's exact words. The בוצע waits until most people finish their אמן, and a ברייתא and בן עזאי teach how to say אמן properly. Two stories ask whether a latecomer can join a זימון and who leads it, and the הלכה is that the greatest person leads even if he came late. Finally the גמרא explains the משנה's foods: one who ate דמאי joins because he could become poor, and מעשר ראשון taken on the stalks is exempt from תרומה גדולה. רב פפא challenges that last rule, and אביי's answer from a פסוק continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The last item in the list: no deferring over dirty hands
steps.stepSummary: This line finishes the ברייתא's list of places where we do not show respect by letting a greater person go first. The last item is dirty hands, meaning hand-washing at the end of the meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not with dirty hands.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud opens at the very end of a ברייתא. Its last case is that we do not insist on letting a greater person go first when washing dirty hands after a meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full ברייתא, which started on the previous amud, says we do not show this kind of respect on roads, on bridges, or with dirty hands. The idea is that in these places, letting someone go first is not a real honor. It only delays people or keeps them uncomfortable. The story that follows will show this rule being used on a road.

keyTerms.meaning: Dirty (greasy) hands, here meaning the washing at the end of a meal (מַיִם אַחֲרוֹנִים)
Showing respect by letting someone go first

phrases.english: and not with dirty hands.
phrases.notes: This is the end of a list that began on the previous amud: not on roads, not on bridges, and not with dirty hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ברייתא that started on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We do not defer to a greater person when washing dirty hands after a meal (nor on roads or bridges).

steps.title: רבין does not let אביי go first on the road
steps.stepSummary: רבין and אביי are traveling. רבין rides ahead without offering to let אביי go first, and אביי privately thinks רבין has become arrogant.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין and אביי were traveling on the road. רבין's donkey went ahead of אביי's, and רבין did not say, 'Let the Master go first.' אביי said to himself: ever since this rabbi came up from ארץ ישראל, he has become arrogant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story that will show the rule we just read being used in real life. This step sets the scene for what comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי expected רבין to step back and honor him. When רבין did not, אביי assumed it was pride, since רבין had recently returned from the great yeshivos of ארץ ישראל. The reader should notice that this happened on a road, which is exactly a place where the ברייתא says we do not defer.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let the Master go first,' a polite way of honoring someone
'The West,' meaning ארץ ישראל (as seen from Bavel)

phrases.aramaic: רָבִין וְאַבָּיֵי הֲווֹ קָא אָזְלִי בְּאוֹרְחָא,
phrases.english: Ravin and Abaye were traveling on the road,
Ravin's donkey went ahead of Abaye's,
and he did not say to him, 'Let the Master go first.'
Abaye said: ever since this one of the rabbis came up from the West (Eretz Yisrael),
phrases.notes: אביי is thinking this to himself.

phrases.english: he has become arrogant.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִין וְאַבָּיֵי הֲווֹ קָא אָזְלִי בְּאוֹרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that shows the ברייתא's rule about roads in action.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story setup: רבין did not defer to אביי on the road.

steps.title: At the בית הכנסת door, רבין defers and אביי asks why only now
steps.stepSummary: At the synagogue entrance רבין tells אביי to go in first. אביי challenges him: wasn't I your Master until now too?
steps.simpleTranslation: When they reached the door of the synagogue, רבין said to him, 'Let the Master enter first.' אביי said to him, 'And until now was I not Master?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבין suddenly shows אביי respect at the doorway. אביי points out the inconsistency: if I deserve honor now, I deserved it on the road too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's question is really a challenge. Either רבין respects him or he doesn't, so why did his behavior change? This sets up רבין's explanation in the next step.

phrases.english: When they reached the door of the synagogue,
Ravin said to him: Let the Master enter first.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְעַד הַשְׁתָּא לָאו מָר אֲנָא?
phrases.english: Abaye said to him: And until now was I not Master?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story. רבין's new behavior leads אביי to challenge him.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבין's inconsistent behavior: he did not defer on the road but did defer at the door.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If אביי deserves honor, he deserved it the whole time, so ignoring him on the road seems disrespectful.

steps.title: רבין explains: we defer only at a doorway with a מזוזה
steps.stepSummary: רבין quotes רבי יוחנן: we show the honor of letting someone go first only at a doorway that has a מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: this is what רבי יוחנן said: we only show this respect at a doorway that has a מזוזה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין answers that he was not being arrogant. He was following a rule from רבי יוחנן that limits this kind of respect to doorways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains both halves of the story. On the road, no deferring is required, which matches the ברייתא. At the doorway, he must defer, so he did. רבין was being careful about הלכה, not proud.

keyTerms.meaning: The scroll fixed to a doorpost

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the respect of going first belongs to a doorway setting, not to every place where two people meet.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: He said to him: thus said Rabbi Yochanan:
One does not defer except
at a doorway that has a mezuzah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A halachic rule that explains the difference in behavior
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי thought רבין ignored him out of arrogance.
steps.terutzMaskana: Deferring applies only at a doorway, so there was no obligation on the road.

steps.title: Challenge: a בית הכנסת has no מזוזה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the wording 'a doorway that has a מזוזה.' Synagogues and study halls have no מזוזה, so would that mean we don't defer there?
steps.simpleTranslation: A doorway that has a מזוזה, yes; one without a מזוזה, no? If so, a בית הכנסת or בית המדרש, which have no מזוזה, would also be places where we don't defer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions רבי יוחנן's rule itself. Taken literally, it does not fit the story, because the story happened at a synagogue door, and synagogues have no מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בית הכנסת is not a home, so it does not need a מזוזה. If the rule depended on a מזוזה actually being there, רבין should not have deferred at the synagogue at all. So the wording must be wrong or too narrow.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But according to this...', a formula that pushes an idea to an unacceptable result

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying a synagogue isn't a real doorway or that honor doesn't belong there. It only questions the exact wording of the rule.

phrases.english: One that has a mezuzah, yes,
one that has no mezuzah, no?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת וּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ,
phrases.english: But according to this, a synagogue and a study hall,
which have no mezuzah,
would it also be that one does not defer there?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רבי יוחנן's rule quoted in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'a doorway that has a מזוזה.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Synagogues have no מזוזה, yet רבין deferred there. A literal reading leads to an unacceptable result.

steps.title: Correction: a doorway fit for a מזוזה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords the rule: we defer at a doorway that is the kind that could hold a מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: at a doorway that is fit for a מזוזה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording. What matters is the kind of doorway, not whether a מזוזה is actually hanging there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A synagogue entrance is a real, built doorway, so it counts even without a מזוזה. A road or a bridge has no doorway at all, so we do not defer there. This fits both the story and the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, say...', which introduces a corrected wording

steps.whatToRemember: We let a greater person go first at a real doorway, one built like a doorway that could hold a מזוזה. We do not need to do this on roads, on bridges, or at the after-meal hand-washing.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
at a doorway that is fit for a mezuzah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge in step 5 by rewording the rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a doorway with an actual מזוזה counts.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any doorway suitable for a מזוזה counts, including a synagogue's.

steps.title: At a meal, guests wait for the one who breaks the bread
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that people eating together may not eat anything until the בוצע has tasted the bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה, son of רב שמואל בר שילת, said in the name of רב: the people reclining at a meal may not eat anything until the one who breaks the bread has tasted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new rule about honor at a meal. The guests must wait for the person who makes המוציא and breaks the bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another case of respect at the table: the guests let the בוצע go first. The word 'anything' means even food other than the bread must wait.

keyTerms.meaning: People reclining (eating together) at a meal
The one who breaks the bread after המוציא

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat, said in the name of Rav:
Those reclining may not eat anything
until the one breaking the bread has tasted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic about showing respect at a meal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Guests may not eat anything until the בוצע tastes the bread.

steps.title: רב ספרא corrects the wording to 'taste'
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא says רב's ruling actually used the word 'taste' (לטעום), not 'eat' (לאכול).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא sat and said: the word that was stated was 'to taste.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא fixes the exact wording of רב's ruling: the word רב used was 'taste,' not 'eat.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ספרא is not arguing with רב. He is reporting the precise word רב used: 'taste' (לטעום) rather than 'eat' (לאכול). Step 9 asks why this matters, and step 10 answers that the law stays the same. Only the wording matters.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's exact word was 'taste' (לטעום). Step 10 explains why רב ספרא insisted on that precise word.

phrases.english: Rav Safra sat and said:
'To taste' is what was stated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects the wording of the ruling in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The exact word רב used was 'taste' (לטעום), not 'eat.' Step 10 explains that the law is the same either way.

steps.title: What difference does the exact word make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between רב saying 'taste' and 'eat'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב ספרא bothered to correct the word from 'eat' to 'taste'. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether we say 'taste' or 'eat', the rule seems to come out the same: nobody eats before the בוצע. So the גמרא wants to know what is gained by insisting on one word over the other.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: For what does it make a difference?
phrases.notes: Asks about רב ספרא's correction in Step 8.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the purpose of רב ספרא's wording correction.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference there is between the version 'to taste' and the version 'to eat'.

steps.title: A student must repeat his teacher's exact words
steps.stepSummary: There is no difference in the law. The point is that a person must quote his teacher exactly.
steps.simpleTranslation: That a person is obligated to say things in his teacher's words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the law does not change at all. רב ספרא corrected the word only because you must repeat your teacher's exact language.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The correction teaches a principle about how תורה is passed down, not a new הלכה about eating. Even when changing a word would not change the law, a student keeps his teacher's wording.

keyTerms.meaning: in the language of his teacher

steps.whatToRemember: 'Taste' and 'eat' lead to the same law. רב ספרא insisted on 'taste' only because a student must quote his teacher word for word.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule about passing down Torah accurately. It shows up in many places in ש"ס.

phrases.english: That a person is obligated to say [it]
phrases.notes: The difference is not about the law itself.

phrases.english: in the language of his teacher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is only in wording. A person must quote his teacher's exact words.

steps.title: Waiting at the shared dish and who reaches first
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that two people sharing a dish wait for each other, but three do not. The בוצע reaches first, but he may let his teacher or a greater person go first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: Two people wait for each other at the dish. Three people do not wait. The one who breaks the bread reaches out his hand first. But if he wants to give honor to his teacher or to someone greater than him, he is allowed to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with more table-manner rules about honor at a meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only two people, if one eats without waiting, the other is left out, so they wait for each other. With three, nobody is left alone, so waiting is not needed. The בוצע has the right to reach first, but he may give that right to someone more important.

keyTerms.meaning: he has permission; it is his choice

steps.confusionAlert: Letting the teacher go first is not required. The ברייתא says הָרְשׁוּת בְּיָדוֹ, meaning the בוצע may do it if he wants.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Two people wait for each other at the dish,
three, they do not wait.
The one who breaks the bread reaches out his hand first,
and if he wants to give honor to his teacher
or to someone greater than him,
he has permission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to new rules about honor at a meal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two people at one dish wait for each other, but three do not. The בוצע reaches first, but he may let his teacher or a greater person go first.

steps.title: Do not break the bread until the אמן is finished
steps.stepSummary: In a story, רבה בר בר חנה teaches his son that the בוצע may not break the bread until everyone answering has finished saying אמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה was busy with his son's wedding at the house of רב שמואל בר רב קטינא. He came early, sat down, and taught his son: The one who breaks the bread may not break it until the אמן has ended from the mouths of those answering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story to bring a new rule: the בוצע must wait until the people answering אמן to his ברכה have finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אמן is treated as part of the ברכה. So the בוצע may not start eating while people are still answering, because the ברכה is not finished yet.

keyTerms.meaning: was busy with his son's wedding

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה הֲוָה עָסֵיק לֵיהּ לִבְרֵיהּ
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana was busy with his son's [wedding]

phrases.aramaic: בֵּי רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב קַטִּינָא,
phrases.english: at the house of Rav Shmuel bar Rav Ketina.
He came early and sat
and taught his son:
phrases.notes: He taught him the laws of the meal before the meal began.

phrases.english: The one who breaks the bread may not break it
until the 'Amen' ends from the mouths of those answering.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה הֲוָה עָסֵיק לֵיהּ לִבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of meal rules with a new halacha told through a story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בוצע may not break the bread until those answering have finished their אמן.

steps.title: רב חסדא: wait only for most of the people
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the בוצע only has to wait until most of the people have finished their אמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: from the mouths of most of those answering.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא makes the rule easier: the בוצע does not need to wait for every last person, only for most of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier rule sounded like it meant everyone answering. רב חסדא limits it to רוב, the majority. Once most have finished, the בוצע may break the bread.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
from the mouths of most of those answering.
phrases.notes: Adds the single word רוב to the earlier rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מִפִּי רוֹב הָעוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the rule from Step 12 to the majority of those answering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בוצע waits only until most of the people answering have finished אמן.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: why is the majority different from the minority?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא challenges רב חסדא: if the ברכה is not finished while most people are still saying אמן, it should also not be finished while a few are still saying it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said to him: What is different about the majority? That the ברכה is not yet finished? With the minority too, the ברכה is not yet finished!
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא attacks רב חסדא's rule of waiting only for most of the people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for waiting is that the ברכה is not complete while people are still answering אמן. That reason applies to the last few people just as much as to most of them. So why stop waiting once the majority is done?

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama said to him:
What is different about the majority?
That the blessing is still not finished?
With the minority too, the blessing is not finished!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's majority rule from Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that the בוצע waits only for most of the people answering.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason for waiting is that the ברכה is unfinished during the אמן. That reason applies to the minority as well, so the majority should not be different.

steps.title: רב חסדא explains why he only waits for most people
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers רמי בר חמא: the few people who are still saying אמן after most have finished are stretching it too long, and that is a mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: I say this because anyone who answers אמן for too long is simply making a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the challenge from step 14. He explains why the בוצע does not have to wait for the last few people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר חמא argued that if the ברכה is not finished while most people are still saying אמן, it should also not be finished while a few are still saying it. רב חסדא answers that the few are not part of the normal ברכה. Once most people have finished, anyone still going is stretching אמן too long, and the בוצע does not need to wait for someone who is doing it wrong.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean a long אמן is always bad. Step 17 (בן עזאי) praises lengthening אמן. רב חסדא is only criticizing someone who stretches it far beyond normal.

phrases.english: He (Rav Chisda) said to him: Because I say,
anyone who answers 'amen' for too long
phrases.notes: He means the few who are still going after most have stopped.

phrases.english: is simply mistaken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רמי בר חמא's challenge in step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the minority's behavior as improper, so their timing does not count
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברכה is not finished until every last person has finished saying אמן
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the normal-length אמן of most people counts; anyone stretching it longer is mistaken and need not be waited for

steps.title: Wrong ways to answer אמן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists three bad kinds of אמן: rushed, cut off, and orphaned. It also warns against tossing out a ברכה carelessly.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One should not answer a rushed אמן, a cut-off אמן, or an orphaned אמן. And a person should not throw a ברכה out of his mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the topic is how to say אמן, the גמרא brings a ברייתא listing the wrong ways to say it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטופה אמן rushes the first part of the word, and a קטופה אמן cuts off the end. A יתומה אמן is said without knowing which ברכה it answers, so it is like an orphan with no parent ברכה. The last rule says a ברכה should not be rattled off quickly and carelessly.

keyTerms.meaning: Rushed, snatched: the first part of אָמֵן is swallowed
Cut off, clipped: the end of אָמֵן is not said fully
Orphaned: an אָמֵן said without knowing which בְּרָכָה it answers
He will throw, meaning to say something carelessly and in a hurry

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין עוֹנִין לֹא ״אָמֵן״ חֲטוּפָה,
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: One does not answer a rushed 'amen',
and not a cut-off 'amen',
and not an orphaned 'amen',
phrases.notes: Said without knowing which ברכה it is answering.

phrases.english: and one should not throw a blessing out of his mouth.
phrases.notes: Do not say a ברכה hastily and carelessly.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין עוֹנִין לֹא ״אָמֵן״ חֲטוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how long to say אמן to the general rules for saying it properly
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אמן must be said fully, clearly, and knowingly, and a ברכה must not be rushed.

steps.title: בן עזאי on the punishment and reward for how one says אמן
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי says each bad kind of אמן brings a matching punishment, and lengthening אמן properly brings long life.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי says: Whoever answers an orphaned אמן, his children will be orphans. A rushed one, his days will be rushed. A cut-off one, his days will be cut short. And whoever lengthens his אמן, his days and years will be lengthened.
steps.whatsHappening: בן עזאי adds a matching consequence to each of the three bad kinds of אמן from the ברייתא. He also gives a reward for saying אמן with care.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each punishment fits the sin by a play on words: יתומה leads to יתומים, חטופה to יתחטפו, and קטופה to יתקטפו. The reward also fits: one who is מאריך his אמן gets מאריכין of his days. Together with step 15, the rule is to lengthen אמן properly, but not too much.

keyTerms.meaning: His days will be cut short

steps.whatToRemember: Say אמן clearly, completely, and knowing which ברכה you are answering. Lengthen it a little for a long-life reward, but not so much that it becomes the mistake from step 15.

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הָעוֹנֶה ״אָמֵן״ יְתוֹמָה —
phrases.english: Ben Azzai says: Anyone who answers an orphaned 'amen'
his children will be orphans,
a rushed one: his days will be rushed away,
a cut-off one: his days will be cut short.
And anyone who lengthens his 'amen'
his days and years are lengthened for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הָעוֹנֶה ״אָמֵן״ יְתוֹמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds consequences and rewards to the ברייתא's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each improper אמן brings a matching punishment, and a properly lengthened אמן brings long life.

steps.title: רב tells a latecomer he cannot join the זימון
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר חייא arrives late and eats quickly to join רב and שמואל. רב tells him it will not help, because they have already finished eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל were sitting at a meal. רב שימי בר חייא came and was eating in a hurry. רב said to him: What are you thinking? Are you trying to join us for a זימון? We have already finished eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of זימון with a story. רב says a person cannot join a זימון with people who have already finished their meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To make a זימון, the people must be eating together. רב believes he and שמואל have already finished, so a newcomer cannot join them. This sets up שמואל's reply in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: To join together, here to complete a זִימּוּן

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel were sitting at a meal.
Rav Shimi bar Chiya came,
and was hurrying and eating.
Rav said to him: What is your thinking?
To join together with us?
phrases.notes: He means joining them for a זימון.

phrases.english: We have already eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of אמן and returns to the laws of eating together and זימון
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב, someone cannot join a זימון with people who have already finished eating.

steps.title: שמואל: we have not really finished eating
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב. If tasty food were brought, they would still eat, so their meal is not truly over and רב שימי can join.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to him: If someone brought me truffles, or young pigeons for Abba (רב), wouldn't we eat them?
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל pushes back on רב's claim that the meal is over. He shows they would still eat if something good were served.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is what counts as finishing a meal. שמואל says a meal is not over just because people stopped eating. As long as they would still eat if more food came, they are still in the middle of the meal, so a latecomer can join their זימון.

keyTerms.meaning: אבא, the personal name of רַב

steps.confusionAlert: Here אבא does not mean 'my father.' It is רב's actual name (רב's name was אבא אריכא), and שמואל is referring to רב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This defines the end of a meal: it is not when eating stops, but when the person truly no longer wants to eat. That decides whether a latecomer can still join the זימון.

phrases.english: Shmuel said to him:
If they brought me truffles,
or young pigeons for Abba (Rav),
wouldn't we eat them?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: of course we would, so the meal is not really finished.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל: אִלּוּ מַיְיתוּ לִי אַרְדִּילַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's claim from step 18 that the meal was over
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב's assumption that they have finished their meal
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Stopping eating does not end the meal while the people would still eat if more food came, so רב שימי can still join

steps.title: רב אחא says the main diner should lead, not the greatest
steps.stepSummary: The students of רב are eating when רב אחא walks in. They want him to lead the blessing because he is a great man. He tells them that one of the main diners leads, not the greatest person.
steps.simpleTranslation: The students of רב were sitting at a meal. רב אחא came in. They said: A great man has come who can lead the blessing for us. He said to them: Do you think the greatest person leads the blessing? The main person of the meal leads the blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a story about a great person who arrives late to a meal. רב אחא says the one who was part of the meal from the start should lead, not him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier story with רב שימי asked whether a latecomer can join at all. This story asks a new question: if a great latecomer joins, does he get to lead? רב אחא says no, because leading belongs to someone who is central to the meal.

keyTerms.meaning: A great man, an important תלמיד חכם
The greatest person present leads the blessing
The main person of the meal, someone there from the beginning

phrases.english: The students of Rav were sitting at a meal.
Rav Acha came in.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי: אֲתָא גַּבְרָא רַבָּא דִּמְבָרֵךְ לַן.
phrases.english: They said: A great man has come who will lead the blessing for us.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְהוּ: מִי סָבְרִיתוּ דְּגָדוֹל מְבָרֵךְ?
phrases.english: He said to them: Do you think that the greatest one leads the blessing?
The main one of the meal leads the blessing.
phrases.notes: Meaning one of the people who ate from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of latecomers to a meal and moves from whether they can join to who should lead.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב אחא, a main participant of the meal leads the blessing, not the greatest latecomer.

steps.title: The halacha: the greatest leads even if he came late
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules against רב אחא. The greatest person present leads the blessing, even if he arrived at the end of the meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is that the greatest person leads the blessing, even though he came at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling. Greatness decides who leads, not when a person arrived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא gave priority to someone central to the meal. The הלכה gives priority to the most honored person, so arriving late does not take away his right to lead.
steps.whatToRemember: In practice, the greatest person at the table leads בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן, even if he only joined at the end.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule for who leads a זימון.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: the greatest one leads the blessing,
even though he came at the end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a final ruling that rejects רב אחא's view.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The greatest person present leads the blessing, even if he arrived at the end of the meal.

steps.title: How can eating דמאי count when it is forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה, which says that someone who ate דמאי can join a זימון. It asks how that works, since דמאי is not fit for him to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If he ate דמאי, and so on, he can join. But it is not fit for him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and challenges one of its cases. A forbidden food should not count toward a זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person cannot make a זימון over food he was not allowed to eat. דמאי may not be eaten until it is tithed, so why does the משנה let him join?

keyTerms.meaning: Produce bought from an עם הארץ that may not have been tithed. The rabbis require tithing it out of doubt.
It is not fit for him, meaning he may not eat it

phrases.english: The משנה said: If he ate demai, etc.
But it is not fit for him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the stories to explain the משנה's list of foods.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that one who ate דמאי joins a זימון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Food that is forbidden to eat should not count for a זימון, and דמאי is forbidden before tithing.

steps.title: He could make himself poor, and then דמאי is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that he could declare all his property ownerless. Then he would be a poor person, and a poor person may eat דמאי, so the food counts as fit for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since, if he wanted, he could make all his property ownerless and become a poor man, then it would be fit for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Because the person has a way to make דמאי allowed for himself, it counts as food that is fit for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is enough that he could become someone who is allowed to eat it. He does not have to actually do it.
steps.confusionAlert: He does not actually have to give away his property. The point is only that he could, and so דמאי counts as potentially fit for him.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאִי בָּעֵי מַפְקַר לְהוּ לְנִכְסֵיהּ
phrases.english: Since, if he wants, he could declare his property ownerless
and become a poor man, and then it is fit for him,

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאִי בָּעֵי מַפְקַר לְהוּ לְנִכְסֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about דמאי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what counts as fit: a food counts if it could become allowed to him
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought דמאי is simply forbidden to him and cannot count.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because he could become poor and be allowed to eat it, דמאי counts as fit, so he joins.

steps.title: Proof: the poor may be fed דמאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from a משנה that poor people may be given דמאי to eat. Soldiers who must be fed by the town may also be given it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: One may feed the poor דמאי, and one may feed soldiers דמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing that a poor person really is allowed to eat דמאי. This supports the previous answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer depended on the idea that a poor person may eat דמאי. This משנה shows that the idea is an accepted rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Soldiers, or guests, whom the town must feed

phrases.english: As we learned: One may feed the poor demai,
and the soldiers demai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 23 with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That a poor person may eat דמאי
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה: מאכילין את העניים דמאי

steps.title: רב הונא: בית שמאי disagree about feeding the poor דמאי
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא cites a ברייתא in which בית שמאי say that the poor and soldiers may not be fed דמאי. This means the משנה follows בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא said: It was taught that בית שמאי say: One may not feed the poor and soldiers דמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a side note that the rule about feeding the poor דמאי is disputed. בית שמאי forbid it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה about זימון with דמאי works only according to בית הלל. For בית שמאי a poor person may not eat דמאי, so the answer about becoming poor would not help.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of שמאי, who often argue with בית הלל

phrases.english: And Rav Huna said: It was taught,
Beit Shammai say: One may not feed
the poor and the soldiers demai.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב הוּנָא: תָּנָא, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the proof by noting that the rule is a dispute, so the משנה follows בית הלל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי forbid feeding the poor and soldiers דמאי, so the משנה follows בית הלל.

steps.title: Why teach the obvious about first tithe?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was taken. It asks why this needs to be said, since the food is clearly permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: First tithe whose תרומה was taken. That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה. It asks why the משנה bothers to teach something that seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If all the gifts have been taken, the food is plainly fine to eat. Why would anyone think it cannot count for a זימון?

keyTerms.meaning: First tithe, given to the לוי
It is obvious, so why teach it?

phrases.english: The משנה said: First tithe whose teruma was taken:
Isn't it obvious?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next food on the משנה's list.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the משנה to mention מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was taken
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Food that has had its gifts taken is obviously permitted, so the line seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The case is a לוי who took his tithe while the grain was on the stalks
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה means a special case. The לוי took his tithe early, while the grain was still on the stalks. He separated תרומת מעשר but not תרומה גדולה. This follows רבי אבהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only where he took it early, while the grain was on the stalks. He separated תרומת מעשר from it but did not separate תרומה גדולה from it, and this follows רבי אבהו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the משנה is teaching a real חידוש. Even this tithe, from which תרומה גדולה was never taken, is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the כהן's תרומה גדולה is taken first and the לוי gets his tithe afterward. Here the לוי got his tithe first, so we might think the missing תרומה גדולה makes it forbidden. The משנה teaches that it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for a special case
He took it early, before the כהן's portion
The main תרומה given to the כהן
The tenth of his tithe that the לוי gives to a כהן

phrases.english: It is needed only where he took it early, while the grain was on the stalks,
and he separated from it the teruma of the tithe,
but he did not separate from it teruma gedola,
and this follows Rabbi Abbahu.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think tithe still missing its תרומה גדולה is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: A tithe taken early on the stalks is exempt from תרומה גדולה, so it is permitted and counts for a זימון.

steps.title: רבי אבהו's source: tithe taken on the stalks is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו, quoting ריש לקיש, says that first tithe taken early on the stalks is exempt from תרומה גדולה. He learns this from the פסוק 'a tithe from the tithe,' which requires only תרומת מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אבהו said in the name of ריש לקיש: First tithe taken early on the stalks is exempt from תרומה גדולה. As it says: 'And you shall set apart from it a gift for ה', a tithe from the tithe.' I told you to give a tithe from the tithe, not תרומה גדולה and also a tithe from the tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the rule it just relied on, together with its source in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק tells the לוי to give only 'a tithe from the tithe,' which is תרומת מעשר. In this case he does not also have to give תרומה גדולה.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall set apart (במדבר יח:כו)

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Abbahu said in the name of Reish Lakish:
First tithe that he took early, while on the stalks,
is exempt from teruma gedola,
as it says: “And you shall set apart from it a gift for ה׳,
a tithe from the tithe”:
A tithe from the tithe I told you,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא תְּרוּמָה גְּדוֹלָה וּתְרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.english: and not teruma gedola and also the teruma of the tithe from the tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes in full the rule that step 27 relied on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First tithe taken on the stalks is exempt from תרומה גדולה, based on 'מעשר מן המעשר'.

steps.title: רב פפא: then exempt it even when taken from the pile
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges אביי. If the פסוק exempts the לוי, then even when he took his tithe early from the grain pile, it should also be exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: If so, even if he took it early from the pile, it should also be exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes the rule further. The same פסוק should seem to exempt a tithe taken from the threshed pile too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו's derivation does not appear to mention stalks. So why limit the exemption to grain on the stalks and not include grain that was already piled up?

keyTerms.meaning: A pile of threshed grain, after it is fully processed

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ הִקְדִּימוֹ בִּכְרִי נָמֵי!
phrases.english: If so, even if he took it early from the pile, it should also be exempt!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: אִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limits of רבי אבהו's derivation.
steps.kashyaTarget: Limiting the exemption to a tithe taken on the stalks
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק's reasoning seems to apply equally to a tithe taken from the pile.

steps.title: אביי begins: a פסוק speaks against you
steps.stepSummary: אביי begins to answer that a פסוק speaks directly against רב פפא's suggestion. The פסוק itself comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: About your case, the פסוק says.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up אביי's answer. He is about to quote a פסוק showing that a tithe taken from the pile is not exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not argue from logic. He says the תורה has a separate פסוק that covers the pile case, and that פסוק continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Against you (about your case) the פסוק says

phrases.english: He said to him: Regarding you, the verse says:
phrases.notes: The פסוק is quoted at the start of the next passage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering רב פפא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A separate פסוק covers the pile case (continued on the next amud)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא thought the exemption should extend to the pile.
steps.terutzMaskana: A פסוק specifically excludes the pile case. Details follow on the next amud.
